references.text: The Lord predicts that Pharaoh will not let the people go, establishing a pattern of Pharaoh's hardness that is repeated throughout the plagues.
The Lord tells Moses that He will harden Pharaoh's heart so that he will not let the people go, the same theme as in 11:9.
God says He will harden Pharaoh's heart and multiply His signs and wonders in Egypt, a direct parallel to the purpose of Pharaoh not listening.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not listen to them, as the Lord had spoken to Moses.
The purpose of allowing Pharaoh to remain was to display God's power and proclaim His name throughout the earth, related to the intent behind the signs.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart to perform His signs among them, so that Israel might tell future generations about it.
Paul quotes God's words to Pharaoh and explains theologically why God hardened Pharaoh's heart—to display His power and proclaim His name.
Both verses link Pharaoh's resistance directly to God's plan to show more wonders and execute judgment.
Moses' doubt about his ability to be heard (6:12) is met by God's confirmation that Pharaoh's opposition is planned for the sake of the signs (11:9).
Both verses connect Pharaoh's resistance directly to God's action through great judgments and the exodus.
Both verses describe God's plan regarding Pharaoh: 6:1 promises deliverance by a mighty hand, while 11:9 explains that Pharaoh's resistance is necessary for the fulfillment of the signs.
Moses' question about how Pharaoh can listen (6:30) is met by God's answer as to why he will not listen (11:9).
